claim.pdf_says: D.19.5.2   Restricting inheritance and modification with the FINAL clause — printed at the same typographic rank as D.19.5.1 Inheritance.
claim.markdown_says: ## D.19.5.2 Restricting inheritance and modification with the FINAL clause  (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:46074) — markdown level 2, while sibling D.19.5.1 is '### D.19.5.1 Inheritance' (:45936).
claim.why_it_matters: A fourth-level clause emitted at markdown level 2 is detached from D.19.5 in the heading tree and sits as a peer of the annex clause D.19 itself.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) Nothing is missing. The kind 'missing-heading' is factually wrong: the heading is present in the transcription at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:46074, verbatim. I read the 300dpi render of page 1145 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1145/spec_p1145.png); the printed glyphs are the bold line 'D.19.5.2   Restricting inheritance and modification with the FINAL clause', and the markdown carries the identical clause number and identical title text. The only textual difference is that the PDF's wide tab gap between the number and the title collapsed to a single space — pure whitespace. All four body paragraphs under the heading are also present and complete (page-1145.md lines 35-41). (2) The PDF offers no evidence for any particular '#' count, and the claim's PDF-side assertion is vacuous. I rendered page 1142 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1142/spec_p1142.png) to check the sibling. The PDF prints 'D.19.5   Other object oriented programming features' and 'D.19.5.1   Inheritance' in the SAME bold face at the SAME size as 'D.19.5.2 ...' on page 1145. ISO flattens annex clause typography: the parent D.19.5 is at the same typographic rank as its own child D.19.5.1, and as its grandchild-level sibling D.19.5.2. Depth is carried solely by the dotted clause NUMBER, not by type size. So 'printed at the same typographic rank as D.19.5.1' is true but proves nothing — by the same test D.19.5.2 is also at the same rank as D.19.5, and no rendering of the PDF can establish that '###' is correct and '##' is wrong. (3) The comparison baseline is cherry-picked, and the claimed convention does not exist. Across Annex D the transcription uses '##' for the large majority of clause headings regardless of nesting depth: '## D.2.2.2', '## D.2.3.2.3', '## D.6.5.6.8', '## D.19.3.3', '## D.19.4.3', and — decisively — the immediate next sibling '## D.19.5.3 Conformance' (:46090) and '## D.19.5.4 Polymorphism' (:46274). D.19.5.2 matches its siblings D.19.5.3 and D.19.5.4; it is '### D.19.5.1 Inheritance' that is the outlier. Picking the one outlier as the baseline manufactures the discrepancy. (4) The stated consequence is not a property of this heading. The file interleaves '## Page NNNN' anchors and a per-page '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' running header ('## Page 1145' at :46043 and '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' at :46045 sit between the code block and this very heading). Heading levels in this transcription are therefore already non-semantic and reset to level 1 at every page boundary; there is no coherent heading tree for D.19.5.2 to be 'detached' from, and '## Annex D' (:41493) is itself only level 2. This is a markdown-formatting artifact of the transcription, not a difference in what the standard says: no text lost, no glyph altered, no meaning changed.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The heading D.19.5.2 'Restricting inheritance and modification with the FINAL clause' is present in full and matches the printed page exactly; only the markdown '#' depth differs, and the PDF prints D.19.5, D.19.5.1 and D.19.5.2 in identical bold type so it cannot adjudicate that depth. At most this is a cosmetic, project-wide heading-level normalization item affecting the majority of Annex D headings (and the page-marker/running-header anchors), not a page-1145 reconciliation defect.
